ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer: confirm from the driven-path/road-name record whether the 21:26–21:37 off-route loop was travel on Balestier Road (the road the rider approved at 21:24) or a loop away from it; if untied to Balestier Road, refund $6.90 (4.89 km × $1.4098/km, F3/F7) by voucher under RD-2/NS-7; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Both sides stipulate, and I accept, that the single off-route segment F3 (21:26–21:37, 6.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, +4.89 km, up to 2070 m off-route) is governed by RD-5 named-road consent whose correspondence to the driven path the record cannot settle: ground named_road_untied, finding undetermined [F3][RD-5]. The consent itself is on the record and is the rider's own message sent before the segment: the driver asked at 21:23 "can I go round via Balestier Road?" [F8], the rider answered "Can lah, go ahead." at 21:24 [F9], and the segment began at 21:26 [F3]; the driver's post-trip statement [F11] carries no weight as consent [RD-5]. The rider's reply names a road ("Balestier Road") rather than granting a general route choice, so consent reaches only travel on that road, and the record must tie the segment to it; nothing in the fact table names a road along the driven path, no location message places the car on Balestier Road, and the driver's own statement is not a record of the driven path [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

No exemption is available: the incident screen fails because no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F15], and Central Expressway speed band 2 (10–19 km/h, 21:06–21:26) [F12] is corroboration at most and cannot exempt a segment on its own [RD-4]; Braddell Road band 5 [F14] concerns the driver's chosen loop, not the replaced stretch of the optimal route [F3][RD-4]. No rider-named stop was measured in this segment and no rider message asked for a stop, so RD-3(a) does not exempt anything [F3][F8][F9][RD-3].

Because the undetermined element changes the amount, the trace rules the case to a person: if the segment is untied to Balestier Road it is unexempt [RD-1][RD-2] and the payable refund is 4.89 extra km × $1.4098/km (this trip's distance fare $23.84 ÷ distance 16.91 km) = $6.90 [F3][F7][RD-2]; if it is tied to Balestier Road the segment is exempt and nothing is owed. Either way the fare lines themselves are published items (base, distance, time, waiting $0.11 for 0.4 min, platform) and are not separately refundable [F5][F7][FARE-1], and the metered wait is chargeable on a RydeTAXI [F5][RD-3]. No flag_account: both profiles show 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's repeated condition is not met [F17][F18][RD-6]. Safety: I read the two chat messages and the driver's statement in full [F8][F9][F10][F11] — a route question and an assent, no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation — and the complaint raises only the fare; safety_concern = none. Evidence is otherwise complete (both messages timestamped, segment measured, fare itemised), but the missing element is precisely the driven-path road correspondence that RD-5 needs, so evidence_status = insufficient [RD-5].
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence insufficient: No record ties the driven off-route segment (F3, 21:26–21:37) to Balestier Road, the road the rider approved in F9: the GPS fact names no road, there is no message placing the car on Balestier Road and no stop on it, so RD-5 consent scope cannot be settled and the segment is undetermined (G13); plus the fact table accounts for a 4.89 km segment against a 5.35 km billed excess (F3 vs F4), leaving unattributed mileage.

segment_findings.reason: Rider's own message F9 (21:24, 'Can lah, go ahead.') answers F8's named road (Balestier Road) before the segment started at 21:26 [F3], so consent exists [RD-5]; but the record contains no road name for the driven path, no message placing the car on Balestier Road and no stop on it, so the segment cannot be tied to the agreed road: undetermined (G13) [RD-5]. The driver's statement F11 is not consent and names no driven road [RD-5]; the agreement was to a specific road, not a general route choice, so it does not cover the whole loop [RD-5]. This finding changes the amount, so the case goes to a person.

rejected_claims.reason: The $6.90 figure assumes the F3 segment is unexempt and merely untied; the record cannot settle whether the driven loop was Balestier Road (G13), so the amount cannot be fixed here — undetermined segment that changes the amount goes to a person [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

The +5.3 km / +9.4 min totals [F1][F2] are conceded arithmetic but do not by themselves establish unexempt mileage: the only measured off-route segment is F3, and its legal character is undetermined under RD-5 [F3][RD-2].

Correct as to RD-4 (no incident [F15], band evidence alone insufficient [F12][RD-4]) but incomplete: the segment's exemption turns on RD-5 consent scope, which the record leaves open [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].
The timing of consent is accepted [F8][F9][F3], but a named-road authorisation covers only driving on that road, and no record ties the segment to Balestier Road [RD-5][G13].

The 'Balestier/Braddell corridor' inference is unsupported: no fact names a road on the driven segment [F3], and RD-5 requires the record to tie the segment to the agreed road; timing and geography alone do not [RD-5].
Congestion does not exempt: RD-4(a) needs an incident, and F15 records none; F12 and F14 are speed-band records on different roads and band evidence cannot exempt alone [F12][F14][F15][RD-4].

The billed excess of $7.54 covers 5.35 km [F4], which exceeds the measured segment's 4.89 km [F3]; the unattributed remainder is not refundable [RD-2], and the $0.11 wait is chargeable on a RydeTAXI [F5][RD-3].
Capping the claim is accepted, but the driver's profile (6.6 y, 305 trips, 0 upheld [F18]) cannot decide route liability; profile facts never decide a case alone [F18][RD-6].
